```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r libs_data}
library(conflicted)
library(tidyverse)
library(car)

df <- read_csv('../../data/unweighted_dataset.csv') |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
```

```{r formulas}
base <- SLD012 ~ RIDAGEYR + RIDAGEYR + RIDRETH3 + DMDEDUC2 + INDFMPIR

f_base <- update(base, . ~ . + ALQ130 + DUQ220U)
f_mental <- update(base, . ~ . + ALQ130 + DUQ220U + DLQ140 + DLQ100)
f_physical <- update(f_base, . ~ . + PAQ670 + PAD680 + BMXBMI)
f_interaction <- update(f_base, . ~ . + DUQ220U:DUQ219 + DUQ220U * ALQ130) # the colon here doesn't add DUQ219 as a main factor
f_interaction_and_physical <- update(f_physical, . ~ . + DUQ220U:DUQ219 + DUQ220U * ALQ130)

f_list <- list(f_base,f_mental,f_physical,f_interaction,f_interaction_and_physical)
```

```{r psych_pairs}
df_less <- df |>
  select(
    SEQN,
    RIDAGEYR,
    RIDRETH3,
    DMDEDUC2,
    INDFMPIR,
    ALQ130,
    DUQ219,
    DUQ220U,
    DLQ140,
    DLQ100,
    PAQ670,
    PAD680,
    BMXBMI
  )

psych::pairs.panels(df_less)
```

```{r model_runs}

models <- vector(mode = "list", length=length(f_list))
for (i in 1:length(f_list)) {
  models[[i]] <- lm(formula = f_list[[i]], data=df)
  print(summary(models[[i]]))
}
```

Currently all of our models have incredibly low R-squared, but we need to look
at the psych plot to determine if there any colinearity. Should also consider
model formulation in more detail than this initial script. We also likely need to
look at the residual plots to see if we need to do some form of transformation.

```{r correlation}
##Pearson correlations for just numeric variables for the moment
cormat = cor(drop_na(df_less[c("RIDAGEYR", "INDFMPIR", "ALQ130", "PAQ670", "PAD680", "BMXBMI")]))
pres <- cor.mtest(drop_na(df_less[c("RIDAGEYR", "INDFMPIR", "ALQ130", "PAQ670", "PAD680", "BMXBMI")]), conf.level = .95)
corrplot.mixed(cormat, lower.col = "black", number.cex = 1,p.mat = pres$p, sig.level = .05) # cross out insignificant coefficient
```
